items.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022
items.q: I can’t write a word to jazz you know. I cannot. I cannot write a word to jazz. Charlie Parker, John Coltrane, I can’t write a word.

ctx.x: What part did your love of jazz play in the construction of your poems?

It’s a difficult question to answer straight on. The thing is that they are entirely different things. Jazz, as stimulus, jazz has a way of keeping that part of the mind that hooks up the, hooks up reason and intuition which basically is what poetry is. They could work that way as jazz as an accompanist. But on the other hand I can’t write to jazz you know. I cannot. I cannot write a word to jazz. I can write to classical music you know but I cannot write to jazz. Charlie Parker, John Coltrane, I can’t write a…

I just noticed that struck me, because I was reading “Dear John Coltrane” your poem, and it says, “In the dead of night I’m writing poetry in another hotel room and J.S. Bach is on the radio.” And I went back and read that again, because the title, “John Coltrane,” and you’re listening to J.S. Bach. It was a nice juxtaposition.
